newsitem.title: USA: Nikkei Inc. launches online U.S. consulting firm.
newsitem.headline: Nikkei Inc. launches online U.S. consulting firm.

text.p: Betting that many Americans doing business in Asia still do not fully grasp the business climate there, Nikkei Business Publications lauched a U.S.-based online consulting company Wednesday.
"Our goal is to help American business executives do business in Asia and be successful at it," said Douglas Kaplan, president of consulting firm Nikkei BP BizTech Inc.
The firm, launched by the giant publishing arm of Nikkei Inc. of Japan, set up shop in Santa Clara, Calif. and on the World Wide Web (http://www.JapanBizTech.com).

Using part-time services of some 20 Nikkei editors in Asia, six employees in Santa Clara will cull articles from Nikkei's 30 business and technology publications and other material from Nikkei research for posting on the Web site.
A second major service of the start-up is seminars, Kaplan said. The first one is planned for February in Silicon Valley and named "Wired into Asia." Four others will follow in 1997.
To generate more revenue, Nikkei BP BizTech is also trying to get advertisers on its Web site and sponsors for its seminars.
Kaplan said the Internet was starting to be a major business tool in Asia, with more business people using it than consumers.
The start-up is being underwritten by Nikkei BP, whose publishing endeavours bring in about $400 million in annual revenues, he said.
